description: Shapes rather than words. A model told to avoid the word 'moreover' will still open three sentences with a participle, still keep every bullet the same length, and still put a passive where a subject belongs. These survive paraphrase in a way a lexicon cannot.
baselineNote: All baselines are default_prior. Calibrate before treating any z-score as a measurement.

features.explanation: Share of sentences in the passive. A proxy without a parser, so it over-counts adjectival participles; the wide baseline reflects that.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for methods and results sections, where the passive is the convention and not a tell.

features.explanation: 'Building on this, ...' 'Having established X, ...' Manufactured connective tissue between sentences that are not connected.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for narrative or literary genres where the construction is idiomatic.

features.skillPattern: Be concrete and specific / protect the specific fact
features.explanation: Distinct nominalised stems, counted once each. Naming a subject repeatedly does not register; a wide vocabulary of abstractions does. This is what AbstractNounDensity should have been for domain prose.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for legal, policy or philosophical genres built on abstraction.

features.explanation: Numbers, dates, percentages and units. The counterweight to abstraction: prose that names quantities is doing work generic synthesis cannot fake.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for reflective or narrative genres where quantities are legitimately absent.

features.explanation: Three coordinated adjectives before a noun: 'fast, reliable, and scalable'. The marketing stack, distinct from any three-item list.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for copywriting genres where the construction is the house style.

features.explanation: Human lists are ragged because the items are different sizes. A generated list arrives pre-balanced.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for reference tables and glossaries, where even items are correct.

features.explanation: Bullets shaped '**Label.** explanation'. One of the strongest single format tells in current model output.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for documentation and release notes, where labelled bullets are the convention.

features.explanation: Headings In Title Case Rather Than Sentence case.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for house styles that mandate title case, including several journals.
